svg.title: The validation loop
svg.desc: Six boxes in a loop. One, predict: run the model on the planned grid and write down its numbers, the pass and fail criteria, the residuals expected, and the old model or an alternative beside them. Two, freeze: commit the file before the run and never edit it; a revision is a new file that says what it has seen. Three, measure: the way the engine runs, on its own clock, and log the machine's clocks, power and processes, with a control. Four, compare: predicted over measured against the criteria, after checking the instrument, the machine and the control. If the cells pass, go to six. If they miss, five, diagnose: an error that tracks one term's share points at a constant, fitted on some cells and held out on the rest; an error that changes with the shape points at a mechanism, measured on its own kernel. Six, pin: the grid becomes a test with bounds, and it is now in-sample; the next claim needs new data, back to one.
svg.text: The validation loop
Every change to the model is an experiment: its prediction is on record before the data that will judge it exists.
1 Predict
run the model on the planned grid; write
down its numbers, the pass/fail criteria,
the residuals you expect to see, and the
old model or an alternative beside them
every number labeled
2 Freeze
commit and push the file before the run,
and never edit it; a revision is a new
file that says which data it has seen
predictions_*_before_
measurement.txt
3 Measure
the way the engine runs: its own clock,
its CUDA graphs, its routing; log the
machine (clocks, power, other processes);
run a control: the same cells again, or
the old model on the same trace
4 Compare
predicted ÷ measured
against the frozen criteria; before
blaming the model, check the instrument,
the machine and the control
5 Diagnose the residual
tracks one term's share of the time:
a constant; fit it on some cells,
hold out the rest
changes with the shape: a mechanism;
measure it on its own kernel
6 Pin
the grid becomes a test with bounds, so
no later change can quietly break it;
misses and controls are pinned too
the grid is now in-sample: the next
claim needs data nobody has looked at
miss
fixed
passes: pin it as it stands
next question, new data
held out: nothing in the model has seen it · fitted: a constant came from it · in-sample: a mechanism was built with it in view ·
recorded: stored when measured, not recomputed, and combines with the others. A grid turns in-sample once the model changes with it in view.
